MENTAL_RULE: Get the data and identify the source
GOAL_PROBLEM: Data is unavailable, scattered, or siloed in multiple sources.
Lack of clarity on columns, data types, and distributions.
Presence of errors, outliers, or inconsistencies of unknown scale.
Unknown correlations or behaviors between variables.

MENTAL_RULE: Decide WHAT goes in and what stays out
GOAL_PROBLEM: Defining scope; avoiding data leakage and structural noise.

MENTAL_RULE: Fix errors and noise without adding info
GOAL_PROBLEM: Improving intrinsic quality by correcting inconsistencies.
Reformatting features so the model can learn efficiently.

MENTAL_RULE: Merge sources into one coherent dataset
GOAL_PROBLEM: Unifying multiple sources into a consistent, aligned dataset.
Preparing data for ML consumption without changing its meaning.
Selecting the model based on the problem type and assumptions.
Fitting the model and finding the optimal parameter set.

MENTAL_RULE: Define how to prove it works
GOAL_PROBLEM: Designing an evaluation strategy to prevent leakage.
Objectively measuring quality based on the specific problem.

MENTAL_RULE: Understand WHAT and WHY it learned
GOAL_PROBLEM: Interpreting results, feature importance, or cluster meanings.
Moving from technical metrics to cost reduction or profit.
Identifying methodological errors or unjustified decisions.
Determining whether to deploy, iterate, or discard the project.
Lack of a clear path to integrate the ML model into the existing business systems.
Handling complex prediction flows where one model's output triggers another without creating latency bottlenecks.

MENTAL_RULE: Track performance and data drift over time
GOAL_PROBLEM: Models degrade silently in production due to concept drift or changing data distributions.
Technical debt and knowledge loss if the data science team leaves the project without proper documentation.
